subject: Re: Unexpected latency surge after variant rollout — Oracletech
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@oracletech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in p95/p99 and 5xxs this morning

Karthik,

Heads up — starting ~08:45 PDT we saw a ~2.5x jump in p95 and a ~6x jump in p99 for our hosted endpoints on Redwood. Error rate (5xx) also spiked briefly. This is impacting our user flows (notably the autocomplete endpoint).

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (autocomplete), /v1/chat (search)
- p95 up from ~240ms -> ~620ms, p99 up from ~420ms -> ~2.7s
- 5xx rate peaked at ~1.9% for ~12 minutes

We rolled a small A/B variant earlier this week (opt-in of ~12% traffic) — wondering if that correlates. Can you confirm if any canary/AB changes were pushed this morning?

Customer impact: live search delays and a handful of timeouts on the mobile app. We need an ETA on a fix or rollback and visibility into root cause.

Thanks,
Daniel
Senior SRE, Oracletech

--
Oracletech Support: support@oracletech.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@oracletech.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in p95/p99 and 5xxs this morning

Forwarding Daniel's alert — they report a significant tail-latency spike and a brief 5xx burst affecting critical endpoints. They suspect an A/B variant (they mentioned ~12% traffic).

Immediate asks:
1) Vivek / infra: start triage on backend (oss-serving/runtime) — check model variant rollout logs, autoscaler behavior, and queue lengths.
2) Lauren / CS: please advise customer-facing messaging and gather any additional logs from their side (traces, sample request ids).
3) Ben: loop in account team for expectations on credits/exec comms if we must rollback.

I think a fast rollback of the variant should be considered if we confirm correlation. Please update here with status every 20–30 mins.

-Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@oracletech.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in p95/p99 and 5xxs this morning

On it — starting triage. Initial checks (5 mins):
- Autoscaling at cluster level is nominal; no large pod churn at 08:45.
- Error logs show increased 502/504 from the frontend LB to serving runtime around 08:46–08:58.
- Queue lengths spiked for the quantized variant (tag: redwood-v4.2-quant) on a subset of nodes.

I'll collect traces and DAP spans, and attach a quick trace bundle in the thread when available. If the variant is the culprit we can roll it back from the control plane in ~8–12 minutes.

—Vivek
SRE Manager
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@oracletech.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in p95/p99 and 5xxs this morning

Quick analysis attached (tail-latency-heatmap.png, model-metrics-q2.csv, dap-trace-20280630.pdf). TL;DR: the A/B variant redwood-v4.2-quant shows markedly higher tail for short-context requests due to cache-miss amplification on our continuous-batching path. Details:
- The variant's KV cache policy increases cold-miss recompute for keys with low locality; with 12% traffic we saw uneven distribution across shards.
- Continuous batching for short tokens combined with higher quantized kernel latencies causes some requests to wait for batch formation, pushing p99 out.
- 5xxs were transient and correlated with queue overflow on two GPU pods that became hot for that variant.

Action recommendation: immediate rollback of redwood-v4.2-quant to restore baseline latency; schedule a controlled re-test with adjusted cache policy and shard affinity.

If we rollback now we expect customer p95/p99 to return to baseline within 5–10 minutes.

--
Olga Petrov
Applied ML — Inference Optimization
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@oracletech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 and 5xxs this morning

Daniel — thank you for the report and for your patience. Summary and next steps:

What we found: Olga's analysis points to the A/B variant (redwood-v4.2-quant) as the likely root cause — cache-miss amplification + batching behavior produced elevated tail latencies and briefly overloaded a couple of pods.

Immediate plan (executing now):
- We are rolling back the redwood-v4.2-quant variant from your traffic pool (control plane rollback underway). Expected customer impact: p95/p99 should return to previous baselines within 5–12 minutes.
- Vivek will monitor autoscaler and queue lengths during rollback.
- Olga will prepare a postmortem with corrective changes (cache policy tuning + shard affinity) and propose a safer canary profile for re-test.
- Ben/Lauren: we will prepare a short customer update and propose a one-time credit for the incident window.

I will update here when rollback is complete and share the short note for you to send to your stakeholders. We apologize for the disruption.

-Karthik
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@oracletech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Jul 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 and 5xxs this morning

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clear plan. We saw metrics start to normalize about 10 minutes after your rollback — p95/p99 are back to baseline and error-rate has dropped to <0.1%.

A couple of asks as we close this out:
- Please share the postmortem and the corrective timeline (when can we expect a safe re-test of the variant?).
- Confirm the credit amount and where that will be reflected on our invoice.

Appreciate the team's responsiveness.

Regards,
Daniel
Senior SRE, Oracletech
